capability_reduction.directive: Stage-1 goal, GLM-5.3-Flash directives (2026-10-15): 'Scope for this stage: ... MoE+MLA/DSA (e.g. L3) with the DSA path restricted to kv_len <= 2051 (dense MLA is exact there)'.
capability_reduction.why_2051: DSA keeps the top 512 complete 4-token pools (2048 tokens) + the <= 3 newest tokens per query; for kv_len <= 2051 every visible token is selected, so dense causal latent attention equals the HF computation exactly (doc/architecture.md section 4). Beyond 2051 the indexer selects a strict subset; dense attention would silently diverge from HF, so tt/indexer.py::check_dense_exact rejects such contexts (allocate_cache, prefill, decode-position validation).

capacity_math_not_limiting.conclusion: One MLA/DSA layer + a 1M-token latent cache for one user is ~5.4 GB on a 32 GiB chip: device DRAM does not limit the context; the bound is the deferred sparse indexer path.

capability_reduction.lifted_by: DSA sparse path: k-pooled indexer key cache (128 values per 4 tokens + <= 3 staged rows), indexer scores (ttnn.experimental.indexer_score_dsa), top-512 pools (ttnn.experimental.topk_large_indices) + tail, sparse latent attention; validated against goldens layer_io/L03,L07/4096,32768 topk.pt. Required before a full-model stage serves contexts > 2051.

batch.evidence: doc/ttnn/01-functional-decoder/pcc_real_weights.jsonl test=batched_paged_decode (layers 0, 4, 3 at B=32; layer 3 at B=4), test=prefill_under_live_trace (B=4)

cache_semantics.kda: per slot: recurrent state S [1, 64, 128, 128] fp32 + the last 3 pre-conv q|k|v rows [1, 3, 24576] bf16; persistent buffers updated only by in-place ttnn.copy; no positional input
cache_semantics.mla: paged latent cache [slots * blocks_per_seq, 1, 64, 512] bf16, blocks_per_seq = round_up(ceil((max_seq_len + 63) / 64), 8) (padded tail of the last chunk + 32-byte page-table sticks); caller page table [slots, blocks_per_seq] int32; continuation starts at multiples of the 64-token page
cache_semantics.decode_inactive_slots: cur_pos[u] == -1 marks slot u inactive (idle, or between the chunks of its own prefill): KDA S and conv rows stay bit-identical, MLA skips the cache write and attention; test_decode_between_prefill_chunks[0,4,3] (doc/ttnn/01-functional-decoder/interleaved_decode.jsonl)
cache_semantics.page_table_refresh: update_page_table rewrites the bound device page table in place at a request boundary (a live decode trace keeps reading the same buffer); exercised under a live trace in test_decode_between_prefill_chunks[3]

prefill.program_signature: depends only on the physical chunk length; prepare_prefill compiles every bucket (once per layer kind and device in the optimized decoder, C-4) before a decode trace is captured; prepare_prefill_traces compiles the traced bucket set

traced.api: OptimizedDecoder.prepare_prefill_traces(cache) -> {bucket: PrefillTrace}; capture_prefill_traces(cache, traces); run_prefill_trace(trace, cache, user_slot, chunk_start, n_valid, chunk=host tensor); prefill_forward_traced(streams, cache, traces, user_slot, start_pos); release_prefill_traces(traces)
traced.bucket_rule: alignment x 2^i up to the 2048-token chunk (OptimizedDecoderConfig.prefill_trace_buckets='pow2'); only buckets <= the cache's reachable chunk are captured
traced.chunk_plan: plan_traced_chunks: full 2048-token chunks, then descending bucket-sized pieces, the last piece (< alignment) padded to the alignment; every chunk is exactly full except the last, whose padding is shorter than the alignment (the eager contract's padding rule); MLA chunk starts stay multiples of the 64-token page
traced.trace_scope: one trace per (layer, bucket); slot-independent: KDA via the scratch recurrent state cache.kda.prefill_S (slot state copied in before / written back with fill_cache after each replay, eager) and the device one-hot slot_mask; MLA via the device chunk / user page tables and chunk start of begin_prefill_chunk
traced.buffers: persistent [1,1,bucket,16384] fp32 input and output per bucket; the trace copies the layer output into the output buffer (valid until the next replay of that bucket)
traced.setup_order: allocate_cache / make_page_table -> prepare_prefill_traces (buffers + one eager run per bucket: every program compiled, every lazy constant built) -> warm + capture decode traces -> capture_prefill_traces; no program compiled and no long-lived buffer allocated after the first capture
traced.trace_lifetime: traces live with the layer's cache; release_prefill_traces frees them and their buffers
traced.evidence: doc/ttnn/03-optimized-decoder/prefill_trace.jsonl, prefill_trace_perf.jsonl (TT_METAL_TRACE_ALLOC_TRACKING=1 TT_METAL_TRACE_ALLOC_SKIP_PROGRAM_CACHE=0 for the correctness rows)

kda_state_accuracy.reference: independent fp32 CPU run (golden streams_in -> attn mHC pre -> input norm -> KDA) over the cycled 1M-token input of tests/test_long_context.py; scripts/f1_cpu_longref.py, scripts/compare_kda_drift.py
kda_state_accuracy.note: The input cycles the golden 32K prompt, so the carried state settles into a periodic regime; the same protocol exposed the pre-fix drift (L1 state PCC 0.986 at 256K, norm ratio 0.947: doc/ttnn/01-functional-decoder/f1_investigation/kda_drift_composite_opdecay.jsonl), so it detects compounding error.
kda_state_accuracy.long_context_resume: layer 4 ran with GLM53_LONG_RESUME_DIR (state checkpoint per 32K call; not needed in the final run: resumed_at_positions = []); resume reproduces an uninterrupted prefill bitwise (doc/ttnn/01-functional-decoder/resume_check.jsonl)

full_model_generator.supported_context: min over layer kinds (backend.supported_context: 2051 while sparse_dsa runs the dense-exact regime, 1048576 once the DSA sparse path lands) and the allocated max_seq_len; requests needing start + prompt + max_new_tokens - 1 positions beyond it raise ValueError at the public API; max_seq_len=None defaults to backend.supported_context only up to MAX_IMPLICIT_SEQ_LEN = 65536 (ValueError above it: pass max_seq_len explicitly)

decode_buckets.rule: one decode trace per width below max_batch plus max_batch; a step replays the smallest width covering its decoding slots (slots 0..w-1); every width compiled before the first capture
decode_buckets.attribute: Glm53Generator.decode_buckets (= decode_widths(max_batch)); serving adapters (09a) pack live requests into the lowest slots when it is non-empty

slots.page_table: one [slots, blocks_per_seq] table shared by the 11 MLA layers; caller rows set per-slot coverage; positions beyond it raise
slots.inactive_rows_backend_requirement: rows with cur_pos == -1 inside a replayed width: the backend zeroes them at the layer boundary (at least MLA output / MoE router input and head input), keeps their router ids out of the fused_experts union and hands the sampler finite logits rows; the generator never consumes them (Stage 2 review C-9; DECISIONS 2026-10-17 ~19:45Z (c))

continuation.kda: from the slot's cache length only (no rewind)

full_model_generator.token_feedback: layer pipeline (1x8 line): embedding on chip 0, final norm + lm_head + sampler (models/common/sampling TTSampling, tt_out_tok) on the last chip; per-step D2H/H2D PCIe-socket hop captured inside the per-chip traces carries the sampled token from the last chip to chip 0's token input (DecodeIO.tokens); no Python per-token copy (doc/DECISIONS.md 2026-10-17 ~21:55Z/~22:15Z). Semantics: DecodeIO.sampled = last sampler step's tokens (the only token buffer the generator reads); DecodeIO.tokens = next step's input, holds step n's samples before step n+1 runs, and a host write between the two steps wins over the hop's value

sampling.device: models/common/sampling (SamplingGenerator/TTSampling), greedy = k1/p0/temp1 with lowest-id tie-break, top-k <= 32 candidates per vocab split (154880 -> 4 x 38720 on one chip)

multichip_decoder.target_mesh: host-8chip 2x4 Blackhole mesh (8 chips, 4 p300a), FABRIC_1D, mesh/glm8_2x4_mesh_graph_descriptor.textproto
multichip_decoder.strategy: layer pipeline (partition.json pipeline8_ring_wrap): no tensor parallelism, so per-device KV cache, KDA state and weights are exactly the single-chip layer's, on the chip running that layer's attention (state) / sublayers (weights); nothing is replicated except the per-chip cur_pos and page-table copies
multichip_decoder.supported_context_reason: unchanged: sparse_dsa dense-exact bound (stage_scope_directive, capability_reduction) — not a multichip / DRAM limit
multichip_decoder.dram_max_context_note: largest per-user context the measured free DRAM of the tightest MLA chip holds at B=1 (free - 2 GiB reserve) / ((1 KiB latent + 256 B DSA indexer keys) x MLA layers on the chip); the B=32 x 2048 caches are already allocated in the measured footprint. The pipeline does not reduce the advertised context: DRAM would hold ~10^6 tokens for one user once the DSA sparse path lifts the 2051 bound

prefill.logical_lengths: any >= 1 (default chunk policy 'plan': plan_traced_chunks(len, 64, buckets) = full power-of-two chunks + one tail < 64 tokens; KDA layers run the tail at round_up(n, 32) rows, MLA at 64; padded rows zeroed at every unit boundary)
prefill.chunk_policy: prefill_forward(chunk_policy='plan') is the default and the device-accepted path; 'auto' / 'padded' (one padded remainder chunk) are opt-in, allowed only when the chunk pads < 32 rows, and that guard (a4355c0ca56) is host-validated only (not device-validated)
prefill.kda_padding_rule: a prefill chunk must never hold a fully padded 32-row KDA recurrence chunk: prepare_chunk_recurrence skips it and leaves its terms unwritten while the scan still adds them to the state -> wrong KDA state handed to decode (Stage 4 v2 post_prefill_state rows; Stage 6 run 3 end-to-end). Fix (state kept across a dead chunk, 90a58532246) device-validated 2026-10-19 02:18Z on one chip and merged (48a1608e8a8); the plan default and the < 32-row guard stay until Stage 6 re-validates 'auto'
prefill.continuation: start_pos multiple of 64 (MLA page); KDA continues from the slot's state
prefill.traced: one trace per (stage, unit, bucket) on per-chip shared ping-pong buffers (2 x 4064 rows x 64 KiB = 508 MiB per chip); chunks flow chip to chip through eager socket transfers

decode.traces: one per (stage, micro-batch group) = per chip (two on chip 0: head + tail); width = the group's max_batch slots (06a's pow2 width traces need the KDA slot-prefix view: Stage 6)
decode.positions: cur_pos [slots] int32 per stage, advanced in-trace by ttnn.plus_one(skip_negative_entries)
decode.page_table: one [slots, blocks_per_seq] int32 per stage holding MLA layers, shared by them, rewritten in place
decode.handoff: send/recv_direct_async inside the per-chip traces, 2 MiB [1,1,B,16384] fp32 per hop, 8 hops per step

Not a DRAM limit (dram_capacity below).
full_model.public_api_bound: Glm53Generator.check_context: start_pos + prompt_len + max_new_tokens - 1 <= 2051 for every public path (ValueError naming both numbers); prompt lengths 1..2051 accepted, non-aligned included

dram_capacity.method: measured allocator view of every chip after the full model's warmup + every trace capture (batch 1, max_seq_len 2051): weights of the chip's layers, KDA state, MLA latent pages, page tables, per-stage positions, stack / prefill ping-pong buffers, chip-0 terminal (embedding 1.27 GB, lm_head 0.68 GB, logits, samplers), trace region 800 MB (outside the allocator's total). Free bytes after a 1 GiB reserve / (MLA layers on the chip x (1024 B latent + 64 B DSA pooled keys) per token) = batch-1 tokens that fit.
dram_capacity.conclusion: batch 1 fits 2,627,888 tokens on the most constrained chip (>= the advertised 1,048,576): device DRAM does not limit the advertised context at batch 1; at batch B the per-user context is bounded by ~2,627,888 / B tokens on that chip (batch x context product), e.g. B=32 -> ~82,121 tokens per user.

batch.evidence: doc/ttnn/06-full-model/tests.jsonl run 20261019T012205Z: full_model/batch32_mixed (32 mixed-length users in fixed slots, early finishers -> inactive rows, duplicates identical), full_model/batch32_paused_slot, full_model/tf_decode_sweep/b32_*, full_model/serving_pool_paging (max_batch 4, 64-block pool)
batch.decode_widths: every width of Glm53Generator.decode_buckets maps to the full-width pipeline decode trace (KDA decodes every slot of its batched state); rows outside the live set carry cur_pos -1 and are untouched

full_model.token_feedback: wrap plan: embedding, final norm, lm_head and the sampler all on chip 0; the sampler trace writes the sampled token directly into the next decode step's token input (tt_out_tok = DecodeIO.tokens) and copies it to DecodeIO.sampled (the buffer the generator reads); no D2H/H2D hop is needed (06a's line-plan socket hop superseded by the wrap plan; semantics of DecodeIO.tokens / sampled unchanged)
full_model.trace_lifetime: per KV cache: 9 per-chip decode traces (head stage incl. embedding, tail stage incl. head), 2 sampler traces (greedy / sample), prefill traces per (stage, unit, bucket); captured once in warmup phase 2, retained until teardown; TT_METAL_TRACE_ALLOC_TRACKING=1 runs clean (runs 20261018T232823Z, 20261019T012205Z; final code: run A of maintenance #2)

vllm_serving.served_max_model_len_note: = current_supported_context (the MLA/DSA dense-exact bound, stage_scope_directive); vLLM refuses a prompt + max_tokens above it with HTTP 400; async look-ahead stays inside it (the last scheduled decode position is 2050). Not a hard physical limit: lifted with the DSA sparse path (capability_reduction.lifted_by).
vllm_serving.kv_cache_dtype: bfloat16 MLA latent (vLLM MLAAttentionSpec per MLA layer, 1024 B/token/layer); KDA state model-owned per slot
